Problem 1
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 35\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal floor. The coefficient of static friction between the crate and the floor is $\mu_s = 0.45$. A horizontal push $P$ is applied low on the crate so that tipping is not a concern. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate on a rough floor with a horizontal push
Determine the smallest horizontal push $P$ that will cause the crate to be on the verge of slipping.
Solution
155 N
Step 1List the givens: $m = 35\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.45$, $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Step 2Compute the weight: $$W = mg = (35)(9.81) = 343.35\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W = 343.35\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 4Apply $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P = F$.
Step 5Motion is impending, so the friction equation applies: $F = \mu_s N$.
Step 6Substitute: $$P = (0.45)(343.35\ \mathrm{N}) = 154.5\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7State the result: $P \approx 155\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 35\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.45$, $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Weight: $W = mg = (35\ \mathrm{kg})(9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}) = 343.35\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N - W = 0$, so $N = 343.35\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P - F = 0$, so $P = F$. At impending slip $F = F_{max} = \mu_s N$: $$P = \mu_s N = (0.45)(343.35\ \mathrm{N}) = 154.5\ \mathrm{N} \approx 155\ \mathrm{N}$$ Units: $\mu_s$ is dimensionless, so the result is in newtons.
Problem 2
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 50\ \mathrm{kg}$ sits on a horizontal floor where $\mu_s = 0.40$ and $\mu_k = 0.30$. A steady horizontal push of $P = 220\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied low on the crate. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate pushed horizontally on a rough floor
Decide whether the crate stays at rest or slides, and determine the friction force that the floor actually exerts on the crate.
Solution
147 N
Step 1Compute the weight and normal force: $$N = W = (50)(9.81) = 490.5\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Find the static limit: $$F_{max} = \mu_s N = (0.40)(490.5) = 196.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Friction required for equilibrium: $F = P = 220\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 4Compare: $220\ \mathrm{N} > 196.2\ \mathrm{N}$, so the crate slips.
Step 5Once sliding, use kinetic friction: $$F_k = \mu_k N = (0.30)(490.5) = 147.15\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6State the result: the crate slides and $F \approx 147\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 50\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.40$, $\mu_k = 0.30$, $P = 220\ \mathrm{N}$. $W = mg = (50)(9.81) = 490.5\ \mathrm{N}$ and $\Sigma F_y = 0$ gives $N = 490.5\ \mathrm{N}$. Maximum static friction: $F_{max} = \mu_s N = (0.40)(490.5\ \mathrm{N}) = 196.2\ \mathrm{N}$. Equilibrium would require $F = P = 220\ \mathrm{N}$, which exceeds $196.2\ \mathrm{N}$, so static friction cannot hold the crate and it slides. While sliding, the friction force is kinetic: $$F_k = \mu_k N = (0.30)(490.5\ \mathrm{N}) = 147.15\ \mathrm{N} \approx 147\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 3
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 40\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a horizontal floor with $\mu_s = 0.35$. A worker pushes on it with a force $P$ directed at $\theta = 25^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. The crate is low and wide, so tipping does not occur. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate pushed by a force angled below the horizontal
Determine the magnitude of $P$ for which slipping is impending.
Solution
181 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (40)(9.81) = 392.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Write $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P\cos\theta = F$.
Step 3Write $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W + P\sin\theta$ (the downward push increases $N$).
Step 4Apply the impending-slip condition $F = \mu_s N$: $$P\cos\theta = \mu_s (W + P\sin\theta)$$
Step 5Solve for $P$: $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta - \mu_s \sin\theta}$$
Step 6Substitute: $$P = \frac{(0.35)(392.4)}{\cos 25^{\circ} - 0.35\sin 25^{\circ}} = \frac{137.34}{0.7584}\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7State the result: $P \approx 181\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 40\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.35$, $\theta = 25^{\circ}$. $W = (40)(9.81) = 392.4\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P\cos\theta - F = 0$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N - W - P\sin\theta = 0$, so $N = W + P\sin\theta$. Impending slip: $F = \mu_s N$. Combining: $P\cos\theta = \mu_s (W + P\sin\theta)$, so $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta - \mu_s \sin\theta} = \frac{(0.35)(392.4\ \mathrm{N})}{0.9063 - (0.35)(0.4226)} = \frac{137.34\ \mathrm{N}}{0.7584} = 181.1\ \mathrm{N} \approx 181\ \mathrm{N}$$ The denominator is dimensionless, so $P$ is in newtons.
Problem 4
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 60\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests in equilibrium on a rough horizontal floor. A horizontal push $P = 120\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied at a height $h = 0.90\ \mathrm{m}$ above the floor. Let $O$ be the midpoint of the base and let $x$ be the distance from $O$ to the line of action of the resultant normal force $N$. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Free-body diagram with the normal force offset by x
Determine the offset distance $x$ of the normal force from the centerline.
Solution
0.183 m
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (60)(9.81) = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 3Take moments about $O$, the middle of the base: $$Nx - Ph = 0$$
Step 4Solve for the offset: $$x = \frac{Ph}{W}$$
Step 5Substitute: $$x = \frac{(120)(0.90)}{588.6} = 0.1835\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 6State the result: $x \approx 0.183\ \mathrm{m}$ toward the front edge.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 60\ \mathrm{kg}$, $P = 120\ \mathrm{N}$, $h = 0.90\ \mathrm{m}$. $W = (60)(9.81) = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma M_O = 0$: $Nx - Ph = 0$, so $$x = \frac{Ph}{W} = \frac{(120\ \mathrm{N})(0.90\ \mathrm{m})}{588.6\ \mathrm{N}} = 0.1835\ \mathrm{m} \approx 0.183\ \mathrm{m}$$ Units: $\mathrm{N \cdot m / N = m}$. The normal force shifts toward the edge the crate would tip about.
Problem 5
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform crate of mass $m = 60\ \mathrm{kg}$ has a base of width $a = 0.80\ \mathrm{m}$. It is pushed horizontally at a height $h = 1.20\ \mathrm{m}$ above the floor. The floor is rough enough that the crate does not slip. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate on the verge of tipping about its front edge
Determine the push $P$ at which tipping is impending.
Solution
196 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (60)(9.81) = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2State the tipping condition: $N$ acts at the edge, $x = a/2 = 0.40\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 3Use $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W$.
Step 4Take moments about the middle of the base: $$N\left(\frac{a}{2}\right) - Ph = 0$$
Step 5Solve and substitute: $$P = \frac{(588.6)(0.40)}{1.20} = 196.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6State the result: $P \approx 196\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 60\ \mathrm{kg}$, $a = 0.80\ \mathrm{m}$, $h = 1.20\ \mathrm{m}$. $W = (60)(9.81) = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$. At impending tipping the normal force acts at the front edge, $x = a/2 = 0.40\ \mathrm{m}$. From $\Sigma M_O = 0$: $Nx - Ph = 0$ with $N = W$: $$P = \frac{W(a/2)}{h} = \frac{(588.6\ \mathrm{N})(0.40\ \mathrm{m})}{1.20\ \mathrm{m}} = 196.2\ \mathrm{N} \approx 196\ \mathrm{N}$$ Units: $\mathrm{N \cdot m / m = N}$.
Problem 6
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform crate of mass $m = 80\ \mathrm{kg}$ has a base of width $a = 0.60\ \mathrm{m}$. A worker pushes horizontally at a height $h = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$ above the floor. The coefficient of static friction is $\mu_s = 0.35$. It is not known in advance whether the crate will slip or tip first. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Slip-or-tip free-body diagram of a pushed crate
Using the assume-solve-check procedure, determine the largest push $P$ that causes no motion, and identify whether slipping or tipping governs.
Solution
235 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (80)(9.81) = 784.8\ \mathrm{N}, \quad N = W$$
Step 2Assume slipping: $$P = \mu_s N = (0.35)(784.8) = 274.7\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Check tipping for that push: $$x = \frac{Ph}{W} = \frac{(274.7)(1.00)}{784.8} = 0.350\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 4Compare with $a/2 = 0.30\ \mathrm{m}$: $x > a/2$ is impossible, so the slipping assumption fails.
Step 5Assume tipping with $x = a/2$: $$P = \frac{W(a/2)}{h} = \frac{(784.8)(0.30)}{1.00} = 235.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Check slipping: $F = 235.4\ \mathrm{N} \le 274.7\ \mathrm{N}$, so the check passes.
Step 7State the result: $P_{max} \approx 235\ \mathrm{N}$, and tipping governs.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 80\ \mathrm{kg}$, $a = 0.60\ \mathrm{m}$, $h = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$, $\mu_s = 0.35$. $W = (80)(9.81) = 784.8\ \mathrm{N}$, $N = W$. Assume slipping: $P = F = \mu_s N = (0.35)(784.8\ \mathrm{N}) = 274.7\ \mathrm{N}$. Check tipping: $x = Ph/W = (274.7)(1.00)/784.8 = 0.350\ \mathrm{m}$, but $a/2 = 0.30\ \mathrm{m}$, so $N$ would lie outside the base. The assumption fails. Assume tipping: $x = a/2 = 0.30\ \mathrm{m}$, so $$P = \frac{W(a/2)}{h} = \frac{(784.8\ \mathrm{N})(0.30\ \mathrm{m})}{1.00\ \mathrm{m}} = 235.4\ \mathrm{N} \approx 235\ \mathrm{N}$$ Check slipping: $F = P = 235.4\ \mathrm{N} \le \mu_s N = 274.7\ \mathrm{N}$. The check passes, so tipping governs.
Problem 7
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate slides across a horizontal warehouse floor at constant velocity while a worker pushes on it with a horizontal force $P = 95.0\ \mathrm{N}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is $\mu_k = 0.28$. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate sliding at constant velocity under a horizontal push
Determine the mass of the crate.
Solution
34.6 kg
Step 1Constant velocity means the crate is in equilibrium: $\Sigma F_x = 0$ and $\Sigma F_y = 0$.
Step 2From $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F_k = P = 95.0\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 3From $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = mg$.
Step 4The surfaces are sliding, so $F_k = \mu_k N = \mu_k m g$.
Step 5Solve for the mass: $$m = \frac{P}{\mu_k g} = \frac{95.0}{(0.28)(9.81)} = 34.59\ \mathrm{kg}$$
Step 6State the result: $m \approx 34.6\ \mathrm{kg}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $P = 95.0\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mu_k = 0.28$. Constant velocity means the forces balance. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P - F_k = 0$, so $F_k = 95.0\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W = mg$. While sliding, $F_k = \mu_k N = \mu_k m g$, so $$m = \frac{P}{\mu_k g} = \frac{95.0\ \mathrm{N}}{(0.28)(9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2})} = 34.59\ \mathrm{kg} \approx 34.6\ \mathrm{kg}$$ Units: $\mathrm{N/(m/s^2) = kg}$.
Problem 8
Lesson 1 — Friction
In a test, a crate of mass $m = 45\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a horizontal concrete floor. A horizontal force applied low on the crate is increased slowly, and the crate is observed to be on the verge of slipping when the force reaches $P = 190\ \mathrm{N}$. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Slowly increasing horizontal pull on a crate at impending slip
Determine the coefficient of static friction $\mu_s$ between the crate and the floor.
Solution
0.430
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (45)(9.81) = 441.45\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = 441.45\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 3Apply $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = P = 190\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 4Slip is impending, so $F = \mu_s N$.
Step 5Solve for the coefficient: $$\mu_s = \frac{190}{441.45} = 0.4304$$
Step 6State the result: $\mu_s \approx 0.430$ (dimensionless).
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 45\ \mathrm{kg}$, $P = 190\ \mathrm{N}$ at impending slip. $W = (45)(9.81) = 441.45\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = 441.45\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = P = 190\ \mathrm{N}$. At impending motion $F = F_{max} = \mu_s N$, so $$\mu_s = \frac{F_{max}}{N} = \frac{190\ \mathrm{N}}{441.45\ \mathrm{N}} = 0.4304 \approx 0.430$$ The newtons cancel, so $\mu_s$ has no units.
Problem 9
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform bar of weight $W = 150\ \mathrm{N}$ leans against a vertical wall. Its lower end $A$ rests on the floor, where $\mu_A = 0.25$, and its upper end $B$ rests against the wall, where $\mu_B = 0.35$. The bar makes an angle $\theta$ with the floor.
Bar leaning against a rough wall on a rough floor
Determine the smallest angle $\theta$ at which the bar will not slip.
Solution
61.3 deg
Step 1Identify the type: slipping is impending at both $A$ and $B$, so $F_A = 0.25N_A$ and $F_B = 0.35N_B$.
Step 2Set directions: $F_A$ points toward the wall and $F_B$ points up.
Step 3Apply $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $N_B = F_A = 0.25N_A$.
Step 4Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $$N_A + (0.35)(0.25)N_A = 150\ \mathrm{N} \Rightarrow N_A = 137.9\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Compute $N_B = 34.48\ \mathrm{N}$ and $F_B = 12.07\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 6Take moments about $A$: $$W\frac{L}{2}\cos\theta = N_B L\sin\theta + F_B L\cos\theta$$
Step 7Solve: $$\tan\theta = \frac{75 - 12.07}{34.48} = 1.825$$
Step 8State the result: $\theta \approx 61.3^{\circ}$; any steeper angle is safe.
Worked Solution
Slipping is impending at both contacts: $F_A = 0.25N_A$ (toward the wall) and $F_B = 0.35N_B$ (upward). $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $N_B = F_A = 0.25N_A$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N_A + F_B = W$, so $N_A + (0.35)(0.25N_A) = 150\ \mathrm{N}$, giving $N_A = 150/1.0875 = 137.9\ \mathrm{N}$. Then $N_B = (0.25)(137.9) = 34.48\ \mathrm{N}$ and $F_B = (0.35)(34.48) = 12.07\ \mathrm{N}$. Moments about $A$ for a bar of length $L$: $W(L/2)\cos\theta = N_B L\sin\theta + F_B L\cos\theta$, so $$\tan\theta = \frac{W/2 - F_B}{N_B} = \frac{75 - 12.07}{34.48} = 1.825, \quad \theta = 61.3^{\circ}$$ The length cancels, and the ratio of forces is dimensionless.
Problem 10
Lesson 1 — Friction
A block is placed on a flat board, and the board is slowly tilted. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the board is $\mu_s = 0.36$. The block is short and wide, so it will slip rather than tip.
Block on a tilting board at the angle of static friction
Determine the angle of static friction $\phi_s$, the incline angle at which slipping is impending.
Solution
19.8 deg
Step 1Resolve the weight on the incline: $F = W\sin\phi$ along the surface and $N = W\cos\phi$ normal to it.
Step 2Apply the impending-slip condition: $F = \mu_s N$.
Step 3Combine: $$W\sin\phi_s = \mu_s W\cos\phi_s \Rightarrow \tan\phi_s = \mu_s$$
Step 4Substitute: $$\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.36)$$
Step 5State the result: $\phi_s \approx 19.8^{\circ}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $\mu_s = 0.36$. On an incline at angle $\phi$, equilibrium along and perpendicular to the surface gives $F = W\sin\phi$ and $N = W\cos\phi$. At impending slip $F = \mu_s N$, so $W\sin\phi_s = \mu_s W\cos\phi_s$ and $$\tan\phi_s = \mu_s \Rightarrow \phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.36) = 19.8^{\circ}$$ The weight cancels, so the result does not depend on the block's mass.
Problem 11
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform crate with a base of width $a = 0.70\ \mathrm{m}$ rests on a horizontal floor where $\mu_s = 0.40$. A horizontal push is applied at a height $h$ above the floor and increased slowly.
Push height that separates slipping from tipping
Determine the push height $h$ at which slipping and tipping become impending at the same time. (Pushes below this height make the crate slip first; pushes above it make the crate tip first.)
Solution
0.875 m
Step 1Write the slipping push: $P_{slip} = \mu_s W$.
Step 2Write the tipping push from $\Sigma M_O = 0$ with $x = a/2$: $$P_{tip} = \frac{W(a/2)}{h}$$
Step 3Set the two equal for simultaneous impending motion: $$\mu_s W = \frac{W a}{2h}$$
Step 4Solve for $h$: $$h = \frac{a}{2\mu_s}$$
Step 5Substitute: $$h = \frac{0.70}{2(0.40)} = 0.875\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 6State the result: $h = 0.875\ \mathrm{m}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $a = 0.70\ \mathrm{m}$, $\mu_s = 0.40$. Slipping is impending when $P = \mu_s N = \mu_s W$. Tipping is impending when $x = a/2$, which from $\Sigma M_O = 0$ gives $P = W(a/2)/h$. Setting the two equal: $\mu_s W = W a/(2h)$, so $$h = \frac{a}{2\mu_s} = \frac{0.70\ \mathrm{m}}{2(0.40)} = 0.875\ \mathrm{m}$$ The weight cancels, so the result holds for any crate mass.
Problem 12
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform crate of mass $m = 30\ \mathrm{kg}$ has a base of width $1.00\ \mathrm{m}$ and rests in equilibrium on a rough horizontal floor. A force $P = 120\ \mathrm{N}$ pushes on its left face, directed to the right and downward at $\theta = 20^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. The force is applied $0.50\ \mathrm{m}$ to the left of the crate's centerline and $0.30\ \mathrm{m}$ above the floor. Let $O$ be the midpoint of the base and let $x$ be the position of the resultant normal force $N$ measured from $O$, positive to the right. Nothing says motion is impending. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Angled push on a crate with the normal force at unknown position x
Solve the equilibrium equations and determine the position $x$ of the normal force.
Solution
0.0397 m
Step 1Identify the type: no apparent impending motion, so solve for $F$, $N$, and $x$ from equilibrium alone.
Step 2Compute the weight: $$W = (30)(9.81) = 294.3\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Resolve the push: $P\cos 20^{\circ} = 112.76\ \mathrm{N}$ and $P\sin 20^{\circ} = 41.04\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 4Apply $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = 112.76\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 5Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $$N = 294.3 + 41.04 = 335.34\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Take moments about $O$: $$(41.04)(0.50) - (112.76)(0.30) + Nx = 0$$
Step 7Solve: $$x = \frac{33.83 - 20.52}{335.34} = 0.0397\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 8State the result: $N$ acts $0.0397\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right of the centerline, inside the base, so there is no tipping.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 30\ \mathrm{kg}$, $P = 120\ \mathrm{N}$, $\theta = 20^{\circ}$. $W = (30)(9.81) = 294.3\ \mathrm{N}$. Components of $P$: $P\cos\theta = 112.76\ \mathrm{N}$ (right), $P\sin\theta = 41.04\ \mathrm{N}$ (down). $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = 112.76\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = 294.3 + 41.04 = 335.34\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma M_O = 0$ (counterclockwise positive): $(41.04\ \mathrm{N})(0.50\ \mathrm{m}) - (112.76\ \mathrm{N})(0.30\ \mathrm{m}) + Nx = 0$, so $$x = \frac{33.83 - 20.52}{335.34}\ \mathrm{m} = 0.0397\ \mathrm{m}$$ The positive sign means $N$ acts about $40\ \mathrm{mm}$ to the right of the centerline, well inside the $0.50\ \mathrm{m}$ half-width, so the crate does not tip.
Problem 13
Lesson 1 — Friction
A block of mass $m = 12\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests without moving on a board inclined at $\theta = 15^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the board is $\mu_s = 0.40$. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Block at rest on an incline
Determine the friction force actually acting on the block.
Solution
30.5 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (12)(9.81) = 117.72\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Recognize that motion is not impending, so $F$ comes from equilibrium, not from $\mu_s N$.
Step 3Sum forces along the incline: $F - W\sin\theta = 0$.
Step 4Substitute: $$F = (117.72)\sin 15^{\circ} = 30.47\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Check the limit: $F_{max} = \mu_s W\cos\theta = (0.40)(113.71) = 45.5\ \mathrm{N}$, which is larger than $F$.
Step 6State the result: $F \approx 30.5\ \mathrm{N}$, directed up the slope.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 12\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\theta = 15^{\circ}$, $\mu_s = 0.40$. $W = (12)(9.81) = 117.72\ \mathrm{N}$. The block is at rest and nothing says motion is impending, so friction is found from equilibrium, not from $\mu_s N$. Along the incline: $F - W\sin\theta = 0$, so $$F = W\sin\theta = (117.72\ \mathrm{N})\sin 15^{\circ} = 30.47\ \mathrm{N} \approx 30.5\ \mathrm{N}$$ Check: $N = W\cos\theta = 113.71\ \mathrm{N}$ and $F_{max} = (0.40)(113.71) = 45.5\ \mathrm{N}$. Since $30.5\ \mathrm{N} \le 45.5\ \mathrm{N}$, the block does stay at rest.
Problem 14
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 55\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a horizontal floor with $\mu_s = 0.30$. A rope attached low on the crate pulls with a tension $P$ directed at $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Tipping does not occur. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Crate pulled by a rope angled above the horizontal
Determine the rope tension $P$ at which slipping is impending.
Solution
159 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (55)(9.81) = 539.55\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Write $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P\cos\theta = F$.
Step 3Write $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W - P\sin\theta$ (the upward pull reduces $N$).
Step 4Apply impending slip, $F = \mu_s N$: $$P\cos\theta = \mu_s(W - P\sin\theta)$$
Step 5Solve for $P$: $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta + \mu_s\sin\theta}$$
Step 6Substitute: $$P = \frac{161.87}{0.8660 + 0.1500} = 159.3\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7State the result: $P \approx 159\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 55\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.30$, $\theta = 30^{\circ}$. $W = (55)(9.81) = 539.55\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $P\cos\theta = F$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N + P\sin\theta - W = 0$, so $N = W - P\sin\theta$. Impending slip: $F = \mu_s N$, so $P\cos\theta = \mu_s(W - P\sin\theta)$ and $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta + \mu_s\sin\theta} = \frac{(0.30)(539.55\ \mathrm{N})}{0.8660 + (0.30)(0.5000)} = \frac{161.87\ \mathrm{N}}{1.0160} = 159.3\ \mathrm{N} \approx 159\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 15
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform rectangular crate has a base of width $a = 0.40\ \mathrm{m}$ and a height $H = 1.20\ \mathrm{m}$. It stands on a ramp whose angle $\theta$ with the horizontal is slowly increased. The coefficient of static friction between the crate and the ramp is $\mu_s = 0.45$. No other forces act on the crate.
Tall crate on a ramp of increasing angle
Determine the smallest ramp angle $\theta$ at which the crate is on the verge of motion, and identify whether it slips or tips.
Solution
18.4 deg
Step 1Resolve the weight on the ramp: $F = W\sin\theta$ and $N = W\cos\theta$.
Step 2Assume slipping, $F = \mu_s N$: $$\tan\theta_{slip} = 0.45 \Rightarrow \theta_{slip} = 24.2^{\circ}$$
Step 3Assume tipping: $N$ acts at the downhill edge of the base.
Step 4Take moments about that edge: $$(W\sin\theta)\frac{H}{2} = (W\cos\theta)\frac{a}{2}$$
Step 5Solve: $$\tan\theta_{tip} = \frac{a}{H} = \frac{0.40}{1.20} \Rightarrow \theta_{tip} = 18.4^{\circ}$$
Step 6Compare: tipping occurs at the smaller angle, and the slip check $0.333 \le 0.45$ passes.
Step 7State the result: motion is impending at $\theta \approx 18.4^{\circ}$, and the crate tips.
Worked Solution
Given: $a = 0.40\ \mathrm{m}$, $H = 1.20\ \mathrm{m}$, $\mu_s = 0.45$. Assume slipping: $F = W\sin\theta$, $N = W\cos\theta$, and $F = \mu_s N$ give $\tan\theta = \mu_s$, so $\theta_{slip} = \tan^{-1}(0.45) = 24.2^{\circ}$. Assume tipping: $N$ acts at the downhill edge, so the line of action of $W$ through $G$ passes through that edge. Moments about the downhill edge: $(W\sin\theta)(H/2) = (W\cos\theta)(a/2)$, so $$\tan\theta = \frac{a}{H} = \frac{0.40\ \mathrm{m}}{1.20\ \mathrm{m}} = 0.3333, \quad \theta_{tip} = 18.4^{\circ}$$ The smaller angle governs. Check at $18.4^{\circ}$: required $F/N = \tan\theta = 0.333 \le 0.45$, so the crate has not slipped. The crate tips at $\theta \approx 18.4^{\circ}$.
Problem 16
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 28\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests in equilibrium on a horizontal floor. A worker leans on it with a force $P = 90.0\ \mathrm{N}$ directed at $\theta = 40^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Downward-angled push increases the normal force
Determine the normal force $N$ that the floor exerts on the crate.
Solution
333 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (28)(9.81) = 274.68\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Find the vertical component of the push: $$P\sin\theta = (90.0)\sin 40^{\circ} = 57.85\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N - W - P\sin\theta = 0$.
Step 4Substitute: $$N = 274.68 + 57.85 = 332.5\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5State the result: $N \approx 333\ \mathrm{N}$, larger than the weight.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 28\ \mathrm{kg}$, $P = 90.0\ \mathrm{N}$, $\theta = 40^{\circ}$. $W = (28)(9.81) = 274.68\ \mathrm{N}$. The vertical component of the push is $P\sin\theta = (90.0)\sin 40^{\circ} = 57.85\ \mathrm{N}$, downward. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N - W - P\sin\theta = 0$, so $$N = 274.68\ \mathrm{N} + 57.85\ \mathrm{N} = 332.5\ \mathrm{N} \approx 333\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 17
Lesson 1 — Friction
A worker of mass $m = 75\ \mathrm{kg}$ stands on a level floor and pushes horizontally on a heavy crate with a force of $250\ \mathrm{N}$. The crate does not move, and the worker's feet do not slide. Treat the worker as a body acted on by the crate's horizontal reaction, the worker's weight, and the floor's normal and friction forces. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Forces on a worker pushing a crate
Determine the minimum coefficient of static friction between the worker's shoes and the floor that keeps the worker from slipping.
Solution
0.340
Step 1The crate pushes back on the worker with $R = 250\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 2Find the friction direction: the shoes would slide backward without friction, so $F$ on the shoes points forward.
Step 3Apply $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = 250\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 4Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $$N = (75)(9.81) = 735.75\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5Impose the no-slip condition $F \le \mu_s N$: $$\mu_{s,min} = \frac{250}{735.75} = 0.3398$$
Step 6State the result: $\mu_s \ge 0.340$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 75\ \mathrm{kg}$, push $= 250\ \mathrm{N}$. By Newton's third law the crate pushes back on the worker with $R = 250\ \mathrm{N}$. Without friction the shoes would slide backward, so friction on the shoes points forward, toward the crate. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = R = 250\ \mathrm{N}$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W = (75)(9.81) = 735.75\ \mathrm{N}$. No slipping requires $F \le \mu_s N$, so $$\mu_{s,min} = \frac{F}{N} = \frac{250\ \mathrm{N}}{735.75\ \mathrm{N}} = 0.3398 \approx 0.340$$
Problem 18
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform crate of mass $m = 50\ \mathrm{kg}$ has a base of width $a = 0.60\ \mathrm{m}$ and a height $H = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$. A rope attached to its top right corner $C$ pulls with tension $P$ directed up and to the right at $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. The lower right corner is $B$. The coefficient of static friction is $\mu_s = 0.40$. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Rope pulling at the top corner of a crate
Determine the largest tension $P$ that causes no motion, and identify whether slipping or tipping governs.
Solution
170 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (50)(9.81) = 490.5\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Assume slipping with $N = W - P\sin\theta$ and $F = \mu_s N$: $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta + \mu_s\sin\theta} = \frac{196.2}{1.0660} = 184.0\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Assume tipping: $N$ and $F$ act at corner $B$.
Step 4Take moments about $B$; the vertical component of $P$ passes through $B$: $$W\frac{a}{2} - (P\cos\theta)H = 0$$
Step 5Solve: $$P = \frac{(490.5)(0.30)}{(1.00)\cos 30^{\circ}} = 169.9\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 6Check slipping at this load: $F = 147.2\ \mathrm{N} \le \mu_s N = (0.40)(405.5) = 162.2\ \mathrm{N}$.
Step 7State the result: $P_{max} \approx 170\ \mathrm{N}$, and tipping governs.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 50\ \mathrm{kg}$, $a = 0.60\ \mathrm{m}$, $H = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$, $\theta = 30^{\circ}$, $\mu_s = 0.40$. $W = (50)(9.81) = 490.5\ \mathrm{N}$. Assume slipping: $P\cos\theta = \mu_s(W - P\sin\theta)$, so $P = \dfrac{(0.40)(490.5)}{0.8660 + (0.40)(0.5000)} = \dfrac{196.2}{1.0660} = 184.0\ \mathrm{N}$. Assume tipping about $B$: $N$ and $F$ act at $B$, and the vertical component of $P$ passes through $B$ because $C$ is directly above $B$. $\Sigma M_B = 0$: $W(a/2) - (P\cos\theta)H = 0$, so $$P = \frac{W(a/2)}{H\cos\theta} = \frac{(490.5\ \mathrm{N})(0.30\ \mathrm{m})}{(1.00\ \mathrm{m})(0.8660)} = 169.9\ \mathrm{N} \approx 170\ \mathrm{N}$$ The smaller force governs. Check slipping at $P = 169.9\ \mathrm{N}$: $F = P\cos\theta = 147.2\ \mathrm{N}$, $N = 490.5 - 84.96 = 405.5\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mu_s N = 162.2\ \mathrm{N} \ge 147.2\ \mathrm{N}$. The check passes, so tipping governs.
Problem 19
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform bar leans against a smooth (frictionless) vertical wall. Its lower end $A$ rests on a rough horizontal floor, and its upper end $B$ touches the wall. The bar makes an angle $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ with the floor and is in equilibrium.
Bar against a smooth wall on a rough floor
Determine the minimum coefficient of static friction at $A$ required to hold the bar in this position.
Solution
0.289
Step 1Draw the free-body diagram: $W$ at midlength, $N_A$ and $F_A$ at the floor, and only $N_B$ at the smooth wall.
Step 2Apply $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N_A = W$.
Step 3Apply $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F_A = N_B$.
Step 4Take moments about $A$: $$W\frac{L}{2}\cos\theta = N_B L\sin\theta \Rightarrow N_B = \frac{W}{2\tan\theta}$$
Step 5Impose $F_A \le \mu_s N_A$: $$\mu_{s,min} = \frac{1}{2\tan\theta}$$
Step 6Substitute: $$\mu_{s,min} = \frac{1}{2\tan 60^{\circ}} = 0.289$$
Step 7State the result: $\mu_s \ge 0.289$ at the floor.
Worked Solution
Let the bar have weight $W$ and length $L$. The wall is smooth, so only $N_B$ acts at $B$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N_A = W$. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F_A = N_B$. $\Sigma M_A = 0$: $W(L/2)\cos\theta - N_B L\sin\theta = 0$, so $N_B = \dfrac{W}{2\tan\theta}$. The friction required is $F_A = \dfrac{W}{2\tan\theta}$, and no slipping requires $F_A \le \mu_s N_A$: $$\mu_{s,min} = \frac{F_A}{N_A} = \frac{1}{2\tan\theta} = \frac{1}{2\tan 60^{\circ}} = \frac{1}{3.464} = 0.289$$ Both $W$ and $L$ cancel.
Problem 20
Lesson 1 — Friction
A block of mass $m = 15\ \mathrm{kg}$ sits on a ramp inclined at $\theta = 35^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction is $\mu_s = 0.25$, which is too small to hold the block by itself. A force $P$ is applied parallel to the ramp, directed up the slope, to keep the block from sliding down. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Holding force on a block that tends to slide down a ramp
Determine the smallest force $P$ that prevents the block from sliding down the ramp.
Solution
54.3 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (15)(9.81) = 147.15\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Set the friction direction: the block tends to slide down, so $F$ points up the slope.
Step 3Sum forces perpendicular to the ramp: $$N = W\cos 35^{\circ} = 120.54\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 4Sum forces along the ramp: $P + F - W\sin\theta = 0$.
Step 5Use impending slip, $F = \mu_s N$: $$P = W(\sin\theta - \mu_s\cos\theta)$$
Step 6Substitute: $$P = (147.15)(0.5736 - 0.2048) = 54.27\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7State the result: $P \approx 54.3\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 15\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\theta = 35^{\circ}$, $\mu_s = 0.25$. $W = (15)(9.81) = 147.15\ \mathrm{N}$. For the smallest $P$, the block is about to slide down, so friction acts up the slope at its maximum value. Perpendicular to the ramp: $N = W\cos\theta = (147.15)(0.8192) = 120.54\ \mathrm{N}$. Along the ramp: $P + F - W\sin\theta = 0$ with $F = \mu_s N$: $$P = W(\sin\theta - \mu_s\cos\theta) = (147.15\ \mathrm{N})(0.5736 - 0.2048) = 54.27\ \mathrm{N} \approx 54.3\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 21
Lesson 1 — Friction
A block of mass $m = 18\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a ramp inclined at $\theta = 20^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, where $\mu_s = 0.30$. A force $P$ parallel to the ramp pushes the block up the slope. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Force needed to start a block moving up a ramp
Determine the force $P$ at which the block is on the verge of sliding up the ramp.
Solution
110 N
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (18)(9.81) = 176.58\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Set the friction direction: impending motion is up the slope, so $F$ points down the slope.
Step 3Sum forces perpendicular to the ramp: $$N = W\cos 20^{\circ} = 165.93\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 4Sum forces along the ramp: $P - W\sin\theta - F = 0$.
Step 5Use impending slip, $F = \mu_s N$: $$P = W(\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta)$$
Step 6Substitute: $$P = (176.58)(0.3420 + 0.2819) = 110.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 7State the result: $P \approx 110\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 18\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\theta = 20^{\circ}$, $\mu_s = 0.30$. $W = (18)(9.81) = 176.58\ \mathrm{N}$. Impending motion is up the slope, so friction on the block points down the slope. Perpendicular to the ramp: $N = W\cos\theta = (176.58)(0.9397) = 165.93\ \mathrm{N}$. Along the ramp: $P - W\sin\theta - F = 0$ with $F = \mu_s N$: $$P = W(\sin\theta + \mu_s\cos\theta) = (176.58\ \mathrm{N})(0.3420 + 0.2819) = 110.2\ \mathrm{N} \approx 110\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 22
Lesson 1 — Friction
A uniform crate of mass $m = 60\ \mathrm{kg}$ has a base of width $a = 0.80\ \mathrm{m}$ and rests in equilibrium on a rough floor. A horizontal push $P = 150\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied at a height $h = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$. A stability gauge reports how much of the tipping limit has been used, defined as the ratio of the normal-force offset $x$ to its limiting value $a/2$, expressed as a percentage. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Normal-force offset compared with the half-width of the base
Determine the percentage of the tipping limit that this push has used.
Solution
63.7 %
Step 1Compute the weight: $$W = (60)(9.81) = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}, \quad N = W$$
Step 2Take moments about $O$: $Nx - Ph = 0$.
Step 3Solve for the offset: $$x = \frac{(150)(1.00)}{588.6} = 0.2548\ \mathrm{m}$$
Step 4Identify the tipping limit: $a/2 = 0.40\ \mathrm{m}$.
Step 5Form the ratio: $$\frac{x}{a/2} \cdot 100 = \frac{0.2548}{0.40} \cdot 100 = 63.7\ \%$$
Step 6State the result: about $63.7\ \%$ of the tipping limit is used, so the crate does not tip.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 60\ \mathrm{kg}$, $a = 0.80\ \mathrm{m}$, $P = 150\ \mathrm{N}$, $h = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$. $W = (60)(9.81) = 588.6\ \mathrm{N}$ and $N = W$. $\Sigma M_O = 0$: $Nx - Ph = 0$, so $x = \dfrac{(150\ \mathrm{N})(1.00\ \mathrm{m})}{588.6\ \mathrm{N}} = 0.2548\ \mathrm{m}$. The tipping limit is $a/2 = 0.40\ \mathrm{m}$. $$\frac{x}{a/2} \cdot 100 = \frac{0.2548\ \mathrm{m}}{0.40\ \mathrm{m}} \cdot 100 = 63.7\ \%$$ Since the ratio is below $100\ \%$, the crate is not tipping.
Problem 23
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 32\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a horizontal floor with $\mu_s = 0.42$ and $\mu_k = 0.33$. A horizontal push is increased slowly until the crate breaks loose and begins to slide. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Friction force versus applied push, showing the drop at slipping
Determine how much the friction force drops at the instant the crate goes from impending motion to sliding.
Solution
28.3 N
Step 1Compute the normal force: $$N = W = (32)(9.81) = 313.92\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2Find the maximum static friction: $$F_{max} = (0.42)(313.92) = 131.85\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Find the kinetic friction: $$F_k = (0.33)(313.92) = 103.59\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 4Take the difference: $$\Delta F = (\mu_s - \mu_k)N = (0.09)(313.92) = 28.25\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5State the result: the friction force drops by about $28.3\ \mathrm{N}$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 32\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.42$, $\mu_k = 0.33$. $N = W = (32)(9.81) = 313.92\ \mathrm{N}$. At impending motion: $F_{max} = \mu_s N = (0.42)(313.92) = 131.85\ \mathrm{N}$. While sliding: $F_k = \mu_k N = (0.33)(313.92) = 103.59\ \mathrm{N}$. $$\Delta F = F_{max} - F_k = (\mu_s - \mu_k)N = (0.09)(313.92\ \mathrm{N}) = 28.25\ \mathrm{N} \approx 28.3\ \mathrm{N}$$
Problem 24
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate rests on a horizontal floor with $\mu_s = 0.40$. A worker pushes on it with a force $P$ directed at an angle $\theta$ below the horizontal. As $\theta$ increases, more of the push goes into pressing the crate against the floor. Tipping does not occur.
Steeply angled push on a crate
Determine the angle $\theta$ at and beyond which no push, however large, can make the crate slip.
Solution
68.2 deg
Step 1Write $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = P\cos\theta$.
Step 2Write $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W + P\sin\theta$.
Step 3Apply impending slip, $F = \mu_s N$, and solve for $P$: $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta}$$
Step 4Note that $P$ becomes unbounded when the denominator reaches zero.
Step 5Set $\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta = 0$: $$\tan\theta = \frac{1}{\mu_s} = 2.5$$
Step 6State the result: $\theta \approx 68.2^{\circ}$; at this angle or steeper the crate cannot be pushed into slipping.
Worked Solution
Given: $\mu_s = 0.40$. Let the crate have weight $W$. $\Sigma F_x = 0$: $F = P\cos\theta$. $\Sigma F_y = 0$: $N = W + P\sin\theta$. Impending slip, $F = \mu_s N$, gives $$P = \frac{\mu_s W}{\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta}$$ As the denominator approaches zero, the required $P$ grows without limit. Setting $\cos\theta - \mu_s\sin\theta = 0$: $$\tan\theta = \frac{1}{\mu_s} = \frac{1}{0.40} = 2.5, \quad \theta = 68.2^{\circ}$$ At this angle and steeper, each added newton of push adds at least as much available friction as it adds horizontal force, so the crate cannot be made to slip.
Problem 25
Lesson 1 — Friction
A crate of mass $m = 40\ \mathrm{kg}$ rests on a horizontal floor with $\mu_s = 0.50$. A horizontal push applied low on the crate is increased until slipping is impending. At that instant the floor exerts on the crate both a normal force $N$ and a friction force $F$, which combine into a single resultant contact force $R$. Use $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.
Resultant of the normal and friction forces at impending slip
Determine the magnitude of the resultant contact force $R$ that the floor exerts on the crate at impending slip.
Solution
439 N
Step 1Compute the normal force: $$N = W = (40)(9.81) = 392.4\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 2At impending slip use $F = \mu_s N$: $$F = (0.50)(392.4) = 196.2\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 3Combine the perpendicular components: $$R = \sqrt{N^2 + F^2} = N\sqrt{1 + \mu_s^2}$$
Step 4Substitute: $$R = (392.4)\sqrt{1.25} = 438.7\ \mathrm{N}$$
Step 5State the result: $R \approx 439\ \mathrm{N}$, tilted from the normal by $\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(\mu_s)$.
Worked Solution
Given: $m = 40\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\mu_s = 0.50$. $N = W = (40)(9.81) = 392.4\ \mathrm{N}$. At impending slip: $F = \mu_s N = (0.50)(392.4) = 196.2\ \mathrm{N}$. $N$ and $F$ are perpendicular, so $$R = \sqrt{N^2 + F^2} = N\sqrt{1 + \mu_s^2} = (392.4\ \mathrm{N})\sqrt{1 + 0.25} = 438.7\ \mathrm{N} \approx 439\ \mathrm{N}$$ $R$ is inclined from the normal by the angle of static friction, $\phi_s = \tan^{-1}(0.50) = 26.6^{\circ}$.
